top.title: PTAD unveils N5bn health scheme, announces N180bn pension payments
top.description: By Victor Ahiuma-Young LAGOS — The Pension Transitional Arrangement Directorate (PTAD) has unveiled a N5 billion health insurance scheme for retirees under the Defined Benefit Scheme (DBS), while announcing over N180 billion in pension-related payments and interventions in the last two years. The Executive Secretary of PTAD, Tolulope Odunaiya, disclosed this on Thursday at a stakeholder engagement forum in Lagos, where she outlined the Directorate’s achievements in pension administration, including the settlement of inherited pension liabilities, payment of pension increment arrears and introduction of digital reforms to improve service delivery. Odunaiya said the N5 billion intervention culminated in the establishment of the PTAD Health Insurance Scheme (PHIS) for DBS pensioners, which was formally unveiled at the event. “Most significantly, we secured funding of approximately N5 billion for a major healthcare intervention, culminating in the establishment of the PTAD Health Insurance Scheme (PHIS) for DBS Pensioners, which we are unveiling today,” she said. She explained that the scheme was designed to address retirees’ healthcare needs, stressing that their welfare extended beyond the regular payment of monthly pensions. “This initiative reflects our recognition that Pensioners’ welfare extends beyond the timely payment of monthly pension entitlements. Access to free, quality, and reliable healthcare is fundamental to their well-being and quality of life,” she added. On pension liabilities, the Executive Secretary disclosed that PTAD had settled over N91.5 billion in inherited obligations, including N25.05 billion paid to 9,675 former employees of the defunct Nigerian Telecommunications Limited (NITEL) and its mobile subsidiary, MTEL, as final settlement of outstanding entitlements. She also said over N60 billion had been paid in arrears arising from the N32,000 pension increment, benefiting more than 150,000 eligible pensioners. In addition, the Directorate paid over N23.8 billion in arrears arising from pension increments of 10.66 per cent, 12.95 per cent, 13.8 per cent and 20.55 per cent, alongside the implementation of corresponding increases in monthly pensions. On pension harmonisation, Odunaiya said PTAD had disbursed over N5 billion in arrears to more than 64,000 eligible pensioners. She added that over 30,000 pensioners had benefited from monthly pension re-computation, with N3.8 billion paid in associated arrears. The Executive Secretary further announced that 726 retirees had been enrolled on the pension payroll, comprising 508 former employees of the Federal Mortgage Finance Limited (FMFL) and 218 retirees of the Federal Mortgage Bank of Nigeria (FMBN). The new beneficiaries attract a combined monthly pension obligation of over N41 million, she said. top.title: 'A level below!' - PSG warned their squad players cannot replace injured stars Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Desire Doue
top.description: FBL-EUR-C1-PSG-ROMA - AFP Paris Saint-Germain face a major attacking dilemma after losing Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Desire Doue for the rest of the season. Following a frustrating 2-2 Champions League draw with Roma, former stars Daniel Xuereb and Emmanuel Petit have raised serious doubts over the squad's depth ahead of the January transfer window. PSG's attacking crisis exposed against Roma PSG's offensive struggles were laid bare on Wednesday night as they were held to a 2-2 draw by Roma in the Champions League. With Kvaratskhelia and Doue both ruled out for the remainder of the campaign, the club's supporting cast failed to step up when needed most. Maghnes Akliouche, Ferran Torres and Mika Godts all endured disappointing outings against the Italian side. Their underwhelming displays immediately prompted concern from former PSG striker Xuereb and ex-Chelsea midfielder Petit, who both questioned whether the current squad can cope without their injured talismans. Xuereb questions quality of PSG's deputies Xuereb, a 1984 Olympic champion, offered a blunt assessment of the players tasked with filling the void. Speaking to Le Parisien , he argued that the replacements simply do not match the match-winning quality that has defined PSG's recent success. "Those who played on Wednesday lacked penetration, one-on-one duels and runs in behind," Xuereb said. "They are excellent players, internationals. But if they don't usually play, there are good reasons for that. When Doue and Kvaratskhelia are there, they are second-string players. They are a level below. "If PSG have achieved what they have over the past two or three seasons, it is thanks to players capable of scoring at any moment. Unfortunately, they are injured." Petit urges January action over cruciate fears Petit shares those concerns and believes PSG must enter the winter transfer market to find an attacking reinforcement. Speaking as a pundit on RMC , he stressed that recovering from cruciate ligament injuries is notoriously difficult, meaning the club must plan beyond the current campaign. "They have to explore every opportunity," Petit said. "When you tear your cruciate ligaments, those are not simple injuries. Rare are the players who have returned to their previous level. So the thinking for next summer can already happen in January. You are only looking at this season, whereas I am looking ahead to next season." Crucial winter transfer window awaits PSG PSG now face a defining period as the January transfer window approaches. With Kvaratskhelia and Doue sidelined for the rest of the season, the club's hierarchy must weigh up whether to pursue an immediate attacking signing or trust the options already at their disposal. If no suitable targets are available mid-season, the pressure will remain firmly on the likes of Akliouche, Torres and Godts to rediscover their sharpness.

top.title: Ohio State vs Michigan: Five reasons the Buckeyes win Saturday
top.description: Ohio State is 7-4. Michigan is 6-5. Neither team is playing for anything but pride on Saturday. They say this is a rivalry game where you throw the records out, and for once both teams might actually like to have that happen because of the disappointing seasons in Columbus and Ann Arbor. But pride is plenty in this rivalry, and this game still means a ton -- it always does. And for all the Buckeyes ' struggles this season, there are real reasons to like them in The Game. Here are five reasons we believe Scarlet and Gray will be the better colors over Maize and Blue. 1. Jeremiah Smith is the best player on the field This one is simple. Ohio State receiver Jeremiah Smith is the Heisman frontrunner , the Big Ten's all-time receiving yards leader , and the most talented player either team has. He's caught 86 passes for 1,482 yards and 17 touchdowns this season. He's scored in eight straight games. Michigan has held him in check in two career games -- eight catches for 75 yards. But Smith is playing the best football of his life right now, coming off a 165-yard, two-touchdown game at Nebraska . The Wolverines can double him. They can bracket him. Sooner or later, he's going to make a play that changes the game. 2. Their leading receiver, J.J. Buchanan, is out for the year with a shoulder injury. Ohio State's defense has had its problems -- 30-plus points in three of the last four games. The energy in Ohio Stadium on Saturday will be about more than a 7-4 team playing a 6-5 team. top.title: Cristian Chivu hails Lautaro Martinez's instant Champions League impact as Inter down Stuttgart
top.description: FC Internazionale Milano v VfB Stuttgart - UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD5 - Getty Images Sport Inter coach Cristian Chivu has highlighted the importance of Lautaro Martinez's return to the scoresheet following a crucial Champions League victory over Stuttgart. The Nerazzurri boss was quick to praise his captain's immediate influence after a difficult period for the Italian giants. Lautaro provides the spark Inter moved within a single point of the Champions League top eight on Tuesday night after a professional performance secured a much-needed victory over Stuttgart . It was a near-perfect European night for the Nerazzurri, who paired a much-needed clean sheet with a victory that moves them within a single point. While the entire squad stepped up, it was the sight of Lautaro finding the back of the net almost immediately after stepping onto the pitch that drew the warmest reaction from his manager. "The goal from the Toro? Beauty, quality, it’s all there. But they are top-level players. Lautaro made everyone happy, the bench, the fans, and also defenders and midfielders," Chivu said, as quoted by La Gazzetta dello Sport . Chivu hails Lautaro's timely confidence boost Following a bruising defeat in Bergamo against Atalanta, Chivu’s side responded with a display defined by tactical discipline and clinical finishing. Luka Sucic impressed in a deep-lying role while Francesco Pio Esposito continued his fine form. Chivu was full of praise for Martinez, noting that while the striker's quality was never in question, the goal serves as a massive psychological boost for the entire squad during this busy period of the European campaign. "I thought you would ask me if the fifth striker is missing… At the moment I have three, all good: Lautaro, after the spell in Bergamo, put some minutes in his legs," Chivu remarked. "Mentally for a striker, scoring is a breath of confidence and self-esteem, even if he didn't need it. I am also happy with Pio and Marcus for what they put on the pitch, I hope they stay at these levels but we are aware of the fact that strikers live for collective and personal joys: we must pay great attention regarding their integrity. There are many games and we need them, we hope Bonny returns soon too." Focus shifts back to Serie A Chivu was quick to pivot the focus back to their domestic responsibilities. top.title: 2026 MVBrewers #6: Aaron Ashby
top.description: ST PETERSBURG, FLORIDA - OCTOBER 27: Aaron Ashby #26 of the Milwaukee Brewers interacts with teammates in the dugout during the eleventh inning against the Tampa Bay Rays in game four of the 2026 World Series at Tropicana Field on October 27, 2026 in St Petersburg, Florida. (Photo by Carmen Mandato/Getty Images) | Getty Images The votes are in for our No. 6 spot in this year’s MVBrewers rankings, and it’s the pitcher who had far and away the best postseason: Aaron Ashby. Ashby garnered 47 of the 79 total votes (59.5%), with the other 32 votes scattered across Garrett Mitchell (12 votes), Trevor Megill (nine votes), Logan Henderson (eight votes), Abner Uribe (two votes), and Robert Gasser (one write-in vote from @jorgejuliomachado). Ashby, still just 28, debuted with the Brewers all the way back in 2021. After beginning his career as a starter, Ashby missed the entire 2023 season due to arm injuries. He returned in 2024, making 14 appearances (two starts) before becoming a staple of Milwaukee’s bullpen in 2025. After a great 2025 season — he made 43 appearances, spanning 66 2/3 innings with a 2.16 ERA, 2.70 FIP, and 76 strikeouts — he was Pat Murphy’s most-used arm in 2026, making 75 appearances, totaling 89 1/3 innings with a 3.12 ERA, 3.11 FIP, and 116 strikeouts. While he had a few shaky moments in the middle of the season (he had a 6.57 ERA across 24 2/3 innings in June and July) and walked opposing hitters at the highest clip of his career (4.1 BB/9), he was a formidable set-up arm to the back of the Brewers’ bullpen, anchored by Abner Uribe and Trevor Megill. Ashby came up especially clutch late in the year, when Uribe missed some time, leaving Milwaukee without their set-up man. Across 24 appearances in August and September, Ashby totaled 28 2/3 innings, allowing just five earned runs (1.59 ERA) and striking out 33 batters. Then came the postseason. Across nine appearances, Ashby spanned 18 innings. What happened in those 18 innings? No runs allowed (breaking a major league record) on five hits and three walks, striking out 20. top.title: Rookie Watch: This Year’s Calder Trophy Race Could Be One for the Ages
top.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect We’re not even two months into the 2026-27 NHL season, and I already have no idea who I’d pick to win the Calder Trophy. Roman Kantserov and Trevor Connelly have been putting up ridiculous offensive numbers, Cole Hutson is threatening to do something only four defensemen have accomplished in the NHL’s modern era, and Jacob Fowler has been incredible between the pipes. And as good as those four have been, I’m not ready to rule out any of Gavin McKenna, Ivar Stenberg or Viggo Björck, either. I figured the Calder Trophy race would be a pretty good place to start Rookie Watch, a new weekly column where I’ll be keeping tabs on some of the NHL’s most interesting rookies throughout the season. Roman Kantserov and Trevor Connelly Are Making Their Presence Felt Kantserov has scored five goals over his past two games, recording his first career NHL hat trick against the Vancouver Canucks on Sunday before scoring twice against the Seattle Kraken on Wednesday. The 22-year-old Russian forward is now up to 15 goals and 20 points through his first 25 NHL games with the Chicago Blackhawks. According to NHL.com, his 15 goals are the most by any Blackhawks player through the first 25 games of a season since 1943-44. top.description: If you've ever wondered what it would be like to be the CEO and co-founder of an upstart wrestling organization, put yourself in Chad Bronstein's shoes a couple weeks back. His company, Real American Freestyle (better known as RAF), was gearing up for its first wrestling event in Abu Dhabi. That meant lots of demands on his time, lots of pre-event meetings, the herding of various cats, etc. Bronstein was in one such meeting when he got word that there was an incident in the hotel lobby. And if you follow combat sports news even a little bit, you already know what that incident was . "We really didn't think they were going to cross paths," Bronstein told me, shaking his head as he explained that the company had meticulously timed fighter arrivals and check-ins to avoid such confrontations. "By no means did we think that was going to happen in the hotel lobby." By now you've probably seen the video of that . Maybe from a couple different angles. Punches were thrown. Blood was spilled. It involved a certain contingent from Dagestan running into another, smaller contingent from Georgia (the country, not the state), whereupon all hell broke loose on the nice marble floors of a luxury hotel. Former UFC champion Merab Dvalishvili ended up blooded and battered . The brothers Nurmagomedov — Usman and Umar — ended up looking at potential six-month prison sentences (later rescinded). RAF was looking at a big problem, both in terms of public relations and in regards to that weekend's event, which was supposed to feature both Dvalishvili and Umar Nurmagomedov in separate matches. Merab Dvalishvili has already competed three times for RAF in 2026. Cooper Neill via Getty Images But Bronstein didn't get this far by sitting around bemoaning the bad hands dealt by fate. As a company, RAF is nothing if not opportunistic. In addition, the Directorate paid over N23.8 billion in arrears arising from pension increments of 10.66 per cent, 12.95 per cent, 13.8 per cent and 20.55 per cent, alongside the implementation of corresponding increases in monthly pensions. nigeria.title: ‘Completely unacceptable’: Kimmich blasts Bayern over Musiala treatment
nigeria.description: Bayern Munich vice-captain Joshua Kimmich has hit out at the club’s hierarchy for pressuring Jamal Musiala to take a pay cut as he struggles with a neurological condition. Speaking after a Champions League defeat at Lille on Wednesday, the Germany skipper — who is Bayern’s captain with Manuel Neuer currently injured — became the latest to criticise the German giants. “Of course, the club always comes first and is bigger than the players, but it is not bigger than the person,” Kimmich said. “It’s completely unacceptable and is not the Bayern way… What’s happening now is something that must not happen in this way. I find it completely incomprehensible.” In August, Musiala collapsed twice on the field in pre-season games and then revealed he was suffering from a “neurological disorder” which can lead to “temporary but treatable seizures”. Musiala played last Friday in his first match since a two-month absence with an unrelated hamstring injury. Moments after the match, long-time club powerbroker Karl-Heinz Rummenigge said the 23-year-old midfielder was unlikely to recapture his previous form and should accept a pay cut. “If he doesn’t return to being the Jamal of old, then we need to have a conversation with his family, with the player, and, above all, with his agency — because, frankly, the current financial figures would no longer be justifiable,” Rummenigge told Sky Germany. Honorary president Uli Hoeness and current club chief executive Jan-Christian Dreesen have made similar statements. Musiala signed a lucrative contract extension in February 2025. According to German media reports, he earns 25 million euros ($27 million) per season, making Musiala the club’s second-highest paid player after Ballon d’Or winner Harry Kane. On Sunday, international players’ union FIFPRO accused Bayern of a “coordinated campaign to put pressure on Musiala and his representatives” to accept a wage cut. “A club of Bayern’s standing should know better,” FIFPRO said in a statement. Kimmich said he understood the club’s position but was critical of the decision to go public. “I think this is something that should be discussed behind closed doors, something you can address with Jamal’s agent or with Jamal himself,” Kimmich said. Kimmich missed several games in October after the sudden death of his father and said he appreciated the support of the club during that time. “In my own situation, the club was incredibly special. You could really feel that this sense of togetherness was being lived out,” Kimmich added. Wednesday’s defeat to Lille ended Bayern’s run as the last club in Europe’s top-five leagues yet to suffer defeat in any competition. nigeria.description: By Chioma Obinna & Juliet Umeh LAGOS — The Lagos State Government, United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF), Nigerian Guild of Editors (NGE) and other stakeholders have called for stronger collaboration among government, the media, private sector and communities to address challenges threatening child survival, education and development in Nigeria. The call was made on Thursday at the 2026 World Children’s Day High-Level Media Symposium in Lagos, themed: “Every Child Alive, Thriving and Learning: A Shared Responsibility.” The event was organised by UNICEF Nigeria in partnership with the NGE and Diamond Awards for Media Excellence (DAME), with participation from Airtel Nigeria and other stakeholders. Speaking at the symposium, President of the NGE, Mr Eze Anaba, said ensuring that Nigerian children survived, received quality education and realised their potential was a collective responsibility that should not be left to government alone. Citing a UNICEF report indicating that 18.3 million Nigerian children were out of school, Anaba described the figure as alarming and called for urgent collective action. “In a country of over 200 million people, 18 million-plus of that population is on the streets, not going to school. It’s not only alarming; it’s a collective responsibility,” he said. He challenged media organisations, private sector players, community leaders and parents to assess their contributions towards addressing the challenge. “Have we reminded the government? Community leaders, have they done their part? Has the media done enough? The private sector, has it done enough?” he asked. Anaba urged stakeholders to develop an action plan with specific commitments, stressing that annual commemorations must translate into measurable improvements in children’s lives. Earlier, UNICEF Chief of Communication, Advocacy and Partnership, Ms Lone Hvass, said Nigeria’s future would be determined by the decisions made today to protect and invest in its children. She said child survival, education and learning were interconnected, noting that children excluded from school were also denied opportunities for protection, participation and the realisation of their potential. “The media does much more than report on children’s issues. Media helps determine which issues receive public attention, which voices are heard, which assumptions are challenged, and which movements are followed through,” Hvass said. She urged journalists to move beyond episodic coverage and headlines to sustained reporting that connects individual experiences with systemic challenges, provides evidence and exposes gaps in policy implementation. Also speaking, Lagos State First Lady, Dr Claudiana Ibijoke Sanwo-Olu, said the welfare of children required sustained commitment from government, parents, caregivers, development partners and the media. nigeria.title: NANS hails FG’s move to manufacture passports
nigeria.description: By Adeola Badru The National Association of Nigerian Students (NANS) has described Nigeria’s move to manufacture its own international passports as a significant step towards ending foreign dependence in the production of a document central to the country’s national identity. The association said the establishment of the National Passport Manufacturing Centre (NPMC) would strengthen Nigeria’s sovereignty, while commending the Minister of Interior, Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo, for spearheading the initiative. NANS President, Akinteye Babatunde Afeez, stated this in a press release issued on Thursday, in which he also praised the minister’s reforms in the passport system and the Ministry of Interior. He described the centre as a historic achievement, noting that Nigeria had never manufactured its own international passports since gaining independence more than six decades ago. “More than six decades after Nigeria gained independence, this is the first time Nigeria will dare to produce her own passport. Under Hon. Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo as the Minister of Interior, Nigeria has taken ownership of a document that represents our identity as a sovereign nation for the first time in our nation’s history,” he said. The students’ body said the initiative, which followed several reforms in the passport system, represented a milestone in the country’s efforts to strengthen its national identity and improve public service delivery. It described the groundbreaking ceremony for the centre as a “grand and laudable achievement”, adding that the development reflected the minister’s commitment to nation-building. NANS also said Tunji-Ojo had changed perceptions about the Ministry of Interior, which it said was previously regarded by some as being largely preoccupied with the declaration of public holidays. “BTO has tremendously changed the narrative of the Ministry of Interior. For a ministry that was largely perceived by many as a ministry whose activities revolved around the declaration of public holidays, his leadership has brought a new face to the ministry,” the statement said. “Today, we have a working ministry delivering on its mandate beyond imagination. This is a remarkable shift that deserves recognition.” The association said reforms introduced in the passport system had also eased the difficulties Nigerians previously encountered in obtaining and renewing international passports. It noted that delays and bureaucratic bottlenecks had made the process difficult for many citizens, but said the minister had changed the situation within less than four years. “For years, Nigerians have had to contend with unnecessary delays, bottlenecks and difficulties in obtaining or renewing their international passports. “However, in less than four years, Hon. nigeria.title: DSS foils kidnap attempt in Lafia, arrests three suspects
nigeria.description: By Soni Daniel Community leaders in Lafia Emirate, Lafia Local Government Area of Nasarawa State, have commended the Department of State Services (DSS) for foiling a kidnap attempt in the area and arresting three suspects in connection with the incident. The leaders praised the DSS operatives for their swift response to a distress call following an attempted abduction at the Isa Mustapha Agwai area of Lafia metropolis. Speaking on behalf of the community leaders, the Mai-angwa (community leader) of Farin Kasa community, Chief Yahaya Mohammed, described the operatives as dedicated and professional in the discharge of their duties. Mohammed said the security operatives arrived within minutes of receiving the distress call after unidentified gunmen invaded the community around midnight and attempted to abduct residents. “Some unidentified gunmen invaded our community and attempted to kidnap residents. We immediately alerted DSS operatives who swiftly arrived at the scene. The operatives exchanged gunfire with the abductors,” he said. He said the intervention had restored residents’ confidence in the security agencies, commending the collaboration between the DSS and other security outfits, including community vigilantes. He urged security agencies to ensure that all suspects arrested in connection with the incident were prosecuted in accordance with the law. Meanwhile, three suspects have been taken into DSS custody over the foiled attack. They were identified as Hassan Musa, 19; Muhammadu Sani Idris, 20; and Sale Umaru Zangba, 47. A source disclosed that Zangba, a cleaner at a primary healthcare centre in the area, allegedly confessed to treating one of the suspects who sustained gunshot injuries during the exchange of fire. The source said the DSS had sustained its operations against kidnapping, arms trafficking and other criminal activities in Nasarawa State. According to the source, the agency recorded another breakthrough about three weeks ago with the arrest of one Bello Abdullahi, a suspected arms courier allegedly on his way to deliver weapons to bandits in Kebbi State. The source also disclosed that a suspected kidnapper was arrested while allegedly collecting ransom from a female resident of Nasarawa State. The source assured that those arrested in connection with the various incidents would face the full weight of the law. nigeria.title: Gunmen kill 16, injure four in overnight attack on Plateau community
nigeria.description: By Golok Nanmwa, Jos No fewer than 16 persons, including women, youths and children, have been killed after gunmen stormed Tafi Gana community, a hamlet of Kyie Ihwien, near Jebbu Miango in Bassa Local Government Area of Plateau State. The attack, according to the Irigwe Development Association (IDA), occurred at about 11:30pm on Wednesday, November 25, 2026, leaving four other persons injured and throwing the community into confusion, fear and panic. The association, in a statement signed by its Public Relations Officer, Sam Jugo, and made available to newsmen in Jos on Thursday, said, “The attackers wielded assault rifles and other dangerous weapons.” “They stormed the community and started shooting sporadically.” It added, “By dawn of Thursday, November 26, 2026, about 16 persons lay dead, while four other survivors were rushed to unknown medical facilities with various degrees of injuries.” The association gave the names of those killed as Moses Oko, 70; Maingwa Zere Rangya, 60; Danladi Ishaku, 45; Luka Danladi, 21; Elisha Luka, 18; David Danladi, 10; Ishaya Goslow, 18; Lami Danladi, 30; Isi Ishaku, 18; Zhime Ngaza, 75; ThankGod Danladi, 18; Gideon Joseph, 25; Ladi Abba, 65; Ruth Istifanus, 20; Mary Keyi, 18; and Lazarus Musa, 13. The statement quoted the traditional ruler of the area, Nggwe Gado Dama, as confirming the incident, adding that the matter had been reported to security agencies. It said, “The matter had been reported to security operatives who were, as at press time, at the scene of the attack.” The association condemned the killings and appealed to residents to remain calm and avoid taking the law into their hands. It said, “The IDA appeals to all natives not to take laws into their hands but allow the security agencies to do the needful to dispense justice to the slain.” The association expressed condolences to the bereaved families and the entire Irigwe nation, praying for the repose of the souls of the victims and God’s comfort for their immediate families. nigeria.title: Mr Latin hands over TAMPAN presidency after eight years
nigeria.description: By Enitan Abdultawab Nollywood actor, Bolaji Amusan, popularly known as Mr Latin, has stepped down as president of the Theatre Arts and Motion Pictures Practitioners Association of Nigeria (TAMPAN) after eight years in office. Amusan handed over the association’s leadership to his successor, Ajala Jalingo, at a transition ceremony, announcing the development in a post on his Instagram page on Wednesday. Sharing a video of the handover, the actor described the occasion as the end of his eight year tenure as the association’s Global President. “Today, I officially handed over the TAMPAN flag to my successor, @ajala_jalingo, bringing my eight-year tenure as Global President to a close,” he wrote. Amusan, who became president in December 2018 following the resignation of his predecessor, Dele Odule, was re-elected unopposed in December 2022 for another four-year term. Although he has left the presidency, the actor will remain involved in the association as a member of its Board of Trustees. “I bow out with gratitude, honour and fulfilment, while embracing a new responsibility as a distinguished member of the prestigious Board of Trustees (BOT) of TAMPAN,” he added. He also expressed confidence in the association’s future under Jalingo’s leadership, saying the change in administration would not affect its commitment to service and development. “Leadership may change, but commitment to service and the growth of TAMPAN remains unwavering,” Amusan said. TAMPAN represents theatre and film practitioners across Nigeria, particularly those in the Yoruba movie industry. The association works to promote members’ interests and welfare, as well as the development of the entertainment sector. Amusan began his acting career in 1988 and is known for his comic roles in Yoruba films. He has also worked as a filmmaker and producer. nigeria.description: Tech billionaire Elon Musk said Wednesday he would give every child in the United States two shares in his SpaceX rocket company, doubling an offer he made last month. “Every child in America will receive two SpaceX shares, one from the company and one from me personally,” Musk said in a post on X, the social media platform he also owns. nigeria.title: The Deposit Takes Seconds but Why Does the Withdrawal Take Days
nigeria.description: When online, especially depositing money can feel almost effortless. When playing games online, a player chooses a payment method, enters their required details and they often see the funds appear in their account within a matter of seconds. When the time comes when the player wants to withdraw their money , it can be a very different experience. The request may remain pending for hours before additional processing and banking delays extend the wait across several days. That contrast naturally causes frustration. If a platform can accept money instantly, why can it not return money at the same speed. The answer involves more than payment technology. Withdrawals move through security checks, internal approval processes, payment providers, and banking systems that deposits may not encounter in the same way. Deposits and Withdrawals Are Not Mirror Images A deposit is designed to confirm that funds are available and can be transferred successfully. Payment networks can authorize many card and digital wallet transactions almost immediately. Once authorization is received, the casino can credit the player’s balance, even if the complete financial settlement happens later. A withdrawal requires the platform to release funds from its own system. Before doing so, the operator may need to confirm the player’s identity, verify account ownership, review transaction history, and check whether promotional conditions have been satisfied. The payment must then be approved and sent through an eligible withdrawal method. This difference means that an instant deposit does not prove that an instant withdrawal is technically or operationally possible. However, it also does not excuse operators that create unnecessary obstacles or fail to communicate their procedures clearly. Verification Can Become the First Bottleneck Identity verification is one of the most common reasons for a delayed withdrawal. Casinos may request proof of identity, proof of address, or evidence showing that the payment method belongs to the account holder. These checks are intended to reduce fraud, prevent unauthorized payments, and meet financial compliance obligations. Problems arise when verification is delayed until a player asks to withdraw. Someone may have deposited and played without interruption, only to discover that documents are required before any winnings can be released. Uploading those documents takes minutes, but manual review may take considerably longer, particularly during weekends or periods of high demand. nigeria.description: US President Donald Trump and NATO chief Mark Rutte urged Russia not to “expand the war” in Ukraine, in a joint statement issued Wednesday after meeting in Florida. The “outstanding” and “very impactful” meeting focused on the wars in Ukraine and Iran, said the statement issued by the White House after the closed-door talks at Trump’s Mar-a-Lago resort. “We also discussed the importance of Russia avoiding any actions that intentionally, or unintentionally, expand the war, and the importance of obtaining a peaceful resolution to the war as rapidly as possible,” the statement added. The joint appeal by Trump and Rutte comes despite the US leader describing Russian President Vladimir Putin as “my friend” during a meeting in China last week. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has taken issue with Trump’s comments on Putin. “For us, he is a killer,” Zelensky told CNN. Rutte was asked about Trump’s comments in an interview with Fox News’ “Fox & Friends” on Wednesday. “What President Trump is doing, also in the meeting in Shenzhen, is testing Putin,” the NATO secretary general said. “How serious is he? Is he willing to come to the negotiating table? Is he willing to really engage in talks. “So let’s keep the pressure on. I think it is working, and we have to keep that going.” Trump, accused by critics of siding with Moscow over Kyiv, said following his meeting with Putin that the Russian leader wants to see the war end by “diplomatic means.” The Florida meeting comes as European nations have expressed a desire to join preliminary talks that have so far only included Ukraine, the United States and Russia. Rutte said any agreement is going to have to include security guarantees for Ukraine. “When the war ends, either with a peace deal, preferable, or if not possible, a long-term ceasefire, we need to make sure that Ukraine has the security guarantees going forward,” he said. “But the most important thing here,” Rutte added, “is that we have to make sure that Ukraine has what it needs to keep the fight going, being so successful and putting that maximum pressure on the Russians.” Trump and Rutte also discussed increasing defense spending, which the US president has pressed European powers to do, the joint statement said. The Florida talks also came as Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth is expected to announce in coming weeks a review of the US force presence in Europe. Photo Credit: Pete Edochie/Instagram Nollywood and the wider African entertainment community are mourning the loss of one of their most respected screen icons, Pete Edochie , MON, who passed away on Wednesday, 25 November 2026,at the age of 79. According to an official statement released on behalf of the family by his eldest son, Leo Pete Edochie , the veteran actor and retired broadcaster departed this life at 12:30 a.m. in Enugu, Nigeria, following a protracted battle with prostate cancer. Born on 7 March 1947 in Zaria, Kaduna State, and hailing from Akamnato, Ifite Nteje in Anambra State, Pete Edochie began his career in broadcasting long before becoming a household name on television and cinema screens. At age 20, in 1967, he joined the Eastern Nigeria Broadcasting Service (ENBS)—later the Anambra Broadcasting Service (ABS)—rising steadily through the ranks to serve as Director of Programmes and Deputy Managing Director. His defining breakthrough came in 1987 when he portrayed the fierce, tragic hero Okonkwo in the Nigerian Television Authority’s (NTA) acclaimed television adaptation of Chinua Achebe ‘s Things Fall Apart. His commanding presence and deep, resonant voice earned him international recognition—including a dedicated delegation interview from the BBC—and cemented his place in Nigerian television history. Over a screen career spanning nearly four decades, Pete Edochie became synonymous with authority,traditional wisdom, and unforgettable Igbo proverbs. Whether playing stern monarchs, principled elders, or complex patriarchs, he delivered every line with unmistakable gravitas. His extensive filmography includes standout appearances in classics and modern hits alike, such as Things Fall Apart (1987), Igodo (1999), Egg of Life (2003), Oracle (2003), Billionaires Club (2003), End of Money (2005), Lionheart (2018)—where he starred as Chief Ernest Obiagu alongside Genevieve Nnaji—Unroyal (2020), and Foreigner’s God (2022). In recognition of his immense contributions to Nigerian arts and culture, he was conferred with the national honour of Member of the Order of the Niger (MON) in 2003 by former President Olusegun Obasanjo,alongside the Africa Magic Viewers’ Choice Awards (AMVCA) Industry Merit Award and lifetime achievement honours from the Africa Film Academy and the African Film Festival (TAFF). entertainment.title: How Mary Akinwola Graduated with a Distinction from Oxford After Receiving Multiple Scholarships
entertainment.description: Mary Akinwola graduated from the University of Oxford after receiving the Chevening and Mastercard Foundation Scholarships. My name is Mary Akinwola. I’m a physiotherapist, a strategy consultant, a healthcare entrepreneur, and I recently graduated from the University of Oxford with a distinction in Health Service Improvement and Evaluation. I have probably said that last part a hundred times since getting my results, and honestly, I don’t think I’m tired of saying it yet. Haha! One thing about me is that I like to be involved. I am sometimes curious about things that have absolutely nothing to do with what I’m supposed to be doing, and I genuinely enjoy working with people. I like organising things, bringing people together, and seeing an idea move forward to get accomplished. So I have known that going to Oxford was never going to be just about getting a master’s degree. Let me explain how I ended up there. I studied Physiotherapy at the University of Ibadan, where I graduated with First-Class Honours. During my undergraduate years, I was involved in quite a lot outside academics: student leadership, journalism, research, community health programmes and advocacy. My involvement in community health exposed me to how differently people experience healthcare depending on where they live, what they can afford and what information they have access to. I loved being a physiotherapist, and that allowed me to interrogate questions that went beyond individual patient care. Why do some people receive good healthcare while others struggle to access even basic services? How do we make healthcare more affordable? What role can technology play? And why do some seemingly good healthcare programmes struggle to produce lasting change? Eventually, I realised I wanted to study and work in a field that constantly seeks to improve health systems. I researched different programmes across the US and UK, hoping to study at institutions that have international audiences where I could build a diverse perspective in health. I came across the MSc in Health Service Improvement and Evaluation at the University of Oxford’s Nuffield Department of Medicine. It aligned with many of my interests, so I applied. sports.title: 'A level below!' - PSG warned their squad players cannot replace injured stars Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Desire Doue
sports.description: FBL-EUR-C1-PSG-ROMA - AFP Paris Saint-Germain face a major attacking dilemma after losing Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Desire Doue for the rest of the season. Following a frustrating 2-2 Champions League draw with Roma, former stars Daniel Xuereb and Emmanuel Petit have raised serious doubts over the squad's depth ahead of the January transfer window. PSG's attacking crisis exposed against Roma PSG's offensive struggles were laid bare on Wednesday night as they were held to a 2-2 draw by Roma in the Champions League. With Kvaratskhelia and Doue both ruled out for the remainder of the campaign, the club's supporting cast failed to step up when needed most. Maghnes Akliouche, Ferran Torres and Mika Godts all endured disappointing outings against the Italian side. Their underwhelming displays immediately prompted concern from former PSG striker Xuereb and ex-Chelsea midfielder Petit, who both questioned whether the current squad can cope without their injured talismans. Xuereb questions quality of PSG's deputies Xuereb, a 1984 Olympic champion, offered a blunt assessment of the players tasked with filling the void. Speaking to Le Parisien , he argued that the replacements simply do not match the match-winning quality that has defined PSG's recent success. "Those who played on Wednesday lacked penetration, one-on-one duels and runs in behind," Xuereb said. "They are excellent players, internationals. But if they don't usually play, there are good reasons for that. When Doue and Kvaratskhelia are there, they are second-string players. They are a level below. "If PSG have achieved what they have over the past two or three seasons, it is thanks to players capable of scoring at any moment. Unfortunately, they are injured." Petit urges January action over cruciate fears Petit shares those concerns and believes PSG must enter the winter transfer market to find an attacking reinforcement. Speaking as a pundit on RMC , he stressed that recovering from cruciate ligament injuries is notoriously difficult, meaning the club must plan beyond the current campaign. "They have to explore every opportunity," Petit said. "When you tear your cruciate ligaments, those are not simple injuries. Rare are the players who have returned to their previous level. So the thinking for next summer can already happen in January. You are only looking at this season, whereas I am looking ahead to next season." Crucial winter transfer window awaits PSG PSG now face a defining period as the January transfer window approaches. With Kvaratskhelia and Doue sidelined for the rest of the season, the club's hierarchy must weigh up whether to pursue an immediate attacking signing or trust the options already at their disposal. If no suitable targets are available mid-season, the pressure will remain firmly on the likes of Akliouche, Torres and Godts to rediscover their sharpness.

sports.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect We’re not even two months into the 2026-27 NHL season, and I already have no idea who I’d pick to win the Calder Trophy. Roman Kantserov and Trevor Connelly have been putting up ridiculous offensive numbers, Cole Hutson is threatening to do something only four defensemen have accomplished in the NHL’s modern era, and Jacob Fowler has been incredible between the pipes. And as good as those four have been, I’m not ready to rule out any of Gavin McKenna, Ivar Stenberg or Viggo Björck, either. I figured the Calder Trophy race would be a pretty good place to start Rookie Watch, a new weekly column where I’ll be keeping tabs on some of the NHL’s most interesting rookies throughout the season. Roman Kantserov and Trevor Connelly Are Making Their Presence Felt Kantserov has scored five goals over his past two games, recording his first career NHL hat trick against the Vancouver Canucks on Sunday before scoring twice against the Seattle Kraken on Wednesday. The 22-year-old Russian forward is now up to 15 goals and 20 points through his first 25 NHL games with the Chicago Blackhawks. According to NHL.com, his 15 goals are the most by any Blackhawks player through the first 25 games of a season since 1943-44. Chicago selected Kantserov 44th overall in the 2023 NHL Draft before watching him develop into one of the most dangerous offensive players in the Kontinental Hockey League (KHL). There hasn’t been much of an adjustment period for him offensively since making the jump to North America. Connelly, meanwhile, entered Wednesday with nine goals and 19 points through 26 games with the Vegas Golden Knights, including seven points over his previous five games. What’s impressed me about Connelly is his ability to create offense with the puck on his stick, using his skating and creativity to open up space for himself and his teammates. He’s also managed to produce at that rate while averaging less than 15 minutes of ice time per game. I’d love to see what he could do with a little more offensive responsibility in Vegas. "We really didn't think they were going to cross paths," Bronstein told me, shaking his head as he explained that the company had meticulously timed fighter arrivals and check-ins to avoid such confrontations. "By no means did we think that was going to happen in the hotel lobby." By now you've probably seen the video of that . Maybe from a couple different angles. Punches were thrown. Blood was spilled. It involved a certain contingent from Dagestan running into another, smaller contingent from Georgia (the country, not the state), whereupon all hell broke loose on the nice marble floors of a luxury hotel. Former UFC champion Merab Dvalishvili ended up blooded and battered . The brothers Nurmagomedov — Usman and Umar — ended up looking at potential six-month prison sentences (later rescinded). RAF was looking at a big problem, both in terms of public relations and in regards to that weekend's event, which was supposed to feature both Dvalishvili and Umar Nurmagomedov in separate matches. Merab Dvalishvili has already competed three times for RAF in 2026. Cooper Neill via Getty Images But Bronstein didn't get this far by sitting around bemoaning the bad hands dealt by fate. sports.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect One of my biggest criticisms of Scott Arniel since he took over as head coach of the Winnipeg Jets has been his reluctance to change his lines. It often felt like he was sending the same combinations over the boards every night regardless of who the Jets were playing, how certain players were performing or what was happening within the game. It was a criticism I had of Rick Bowness, too, and at times I wondered how much of it was coming from above the coaching staff. When you see some of the same tendencies carry over from one coach to the next, I think it’s fair to question how much of it is an organizational philosophy rather than an individual coaching preference. Whatever the case may be, I’ve really liked what I’ve seen from Arniel lately. The Jets have now won nine of their past 11 games following a 4-2 victory over the Boston Bruins Wednesday, and Arniel deserves some credit for his willingness to try different things throughout the lineup. Morgan Barron scored the game-winning goal for the second consecutive game Wednesday, and how he found himself on the ice with Cole Perfetti and Dawson Mercer is a great example of the growth we’re seeing from Arniel as a head coach. Scott Arniel Is Getting More Out of His Lineup Barron’s game-winning goal against the Utah Mammoth on Monday came courtesy of a beautiful pass from Viggo Björck, but he found himself centering the fourth line between Cole Koepke and Tyrel Bauer at Wednesday’s morning skate. Arniel wasn’t married to the combinations he put together that morning either, though. Perfetti and Mercer spent 6:44 alongside Brayden Yager and another 4:03 alongside Barron, who ended up scoring the game-winning goal after Arniel put him out with the two forwards for an offensive-zone faceoff late in the second period. I don’t necessarily want Barron permanently occupying a top-six center spot, but there’s nothing wrong with putting him there when Arniel sees an opportunity to get something out of that combination. There’s no reason the Jets need to have the exact same third line on the road without last change against Boston as they do at home with last change against Utah, either. Different teams present different challenges, and Winnipeg has enough versatile forwards to give Arniel some options. There’s something to be said for establishing chemistry and giving players an opportunity to get comfortable playing together, but that doesn’t mean you can’t experiment with different combinations throughout a game. Carter Stadium in Fort Worth, Texas. (Photo by Matthew Pearce/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images We’ve reached the final full Big 12 slate of the 2026 season. All 16 teams are in action. Championship stakes are on the line for three teams. College Football Playoff stakes are also on the line for the same triumvirate. And it all starts on Turkey Day, as the Big 12 is home to the lone college showcase on Thanksgiving. Before previewing the Week 13 matchups, here are the Big 12 Championship Game clinching scenarios for Week 13. Utah (11-0, 8-0 Big 12) Already clinched a spot Texas Tech (10-1, 7-1 Big 12) Clinches with win over TCU or BYU loss to Cincinnati BYU (9-2, 6-2 Big 12) Clinches with win over Cincinnati and Texas Tech loss to TCU Compared to other conferences, this is pretty simple, right? If BYU and Texas Tech both finish 7-2 in conference play, the Cougars get the edge due to the common opponent tiebreaker. Texas Tech would have losses to Cincinnati and TCU, which were teams BYU would have defeated. Meanwhile, the Red Raiders did not face UCF or Utah, the two teams that already defeated the Cougars. As for the CFP picture, Utah is No. 2, BYU is No. 10, and Texas Tech is No. 11. While all three are currently situated within the 12-team bracket, all three aren’t necessarily in the clear with a victory. The Big Ten champion receives an automatic bid this year, and five of the six possible champions are currently ranked below No. 11 — No. 12 Oregon, No. 13 Iowa, No. 14 Indiana, No. 15 USC, and No. 21 Ohio State. The ideal scenario for a three-bid Big 12 is either (a) No. 9 UCLA defeats USC this weekend and subsequently wins the Big Ten Championship Game, or (b) UCLA loses to USC this weekend, falls below No. 11, and the Big Ten champion secures the only playoff bid from the conference. technology.title: UK government working 'around the clock' on Capita contingency plans
technology.description: The UK government is working "around the clock" on contingency plans for Capita contracts after the outsourcer's CEO quit and its shares plunged, a Cabinet Office minister told MPs. Capita announced plans this week to raise around £190 million through a share issue in the first half of 2027 after warning of sharply lower profits and further costs linked to its Civil Service Pension Scheme (CSPS) contract. The outsourcer "should be absolutely ashamed of its performance" on the £239 million contract , Sally Jameson, parliamentary secretary in the Cabinet Office, told MPs on Tuesday . "We have seen evidence that it has stepped up in recent months and begun to rectify the problem, but it is inexcusable that it let the situation get to this point," she said. Adolfo Hernandez stepped down as CEO with immediate effect on Monday, with finance chief Pablo Andres taking over. Shares fell around 70 percent following the announcement. In the House of Commons, Jameson was asked about the government's plans if Capita were unable to carry out the remainder of its contract given the outsourcer's performance on the CSPS. "On contingency planning, it is important that we stabilize the situation and that Capita can continue to deliver the pension scheme. However, the government is working across departments, as we do in relation to all strategic suppliers, to ensure that the relevant contingency plans are in place. People are working around the clock on that," she said. Jameson said contingency planning for the pension scheme was already underway before Monday's announcement, describing it as standard practice for major government suppliers. She told the Chamber that the Cabinet Office was "currently arranging to meet the new CEO in the coming days" following Hernandez's departure. The Register first exposed problems with Capita's CSPS portal last December. The site, serving 1.5 million current and former public servants, rejected login details even for newly created accounts, contained broken and circular links, and displayed dummy text. In January this year, the Cabinet Office was forced to promise "interim support measures" for the CSPS following Capita's botched takeover, including 150 additional government staff to clear the backlog in cases. Speaking in Parliament, Conservative MP Geoffrey Clifton-Brown, chair of the Public Accounts Committee, said there had been "some tragic and dreadful cases" since Capita took over administration last December. "I heard of one poor lady who was living on benefits because she could not get the bereavement payments she needed after her sister's death. technology.title: Hackers help themselves to 1Password's source code and customer data
technology.description: 1Password is reassuring customers that their vaults remain secure after an attacker breached its systems and stole account information and private source code. The Canadian security biz disclosed this week that an attacker had compromised an employee's corporate GitHub account, made off with private source code, and deployed malicious code to its backend services to siphon off customer information. 1Password, which began investigating the intrusion on November 19, hasn't said how many customers were affected, but confirmed that the stolen data includes names and email addresses used to sign in to the service, account identifiers, timestamps showing when users created and last accessed their accounts, and various pieces of non-secret account metadata. The company insists the information that customers actually pay it to protect was beyond the intruder's reach. "At no time were customer vault contents accessed by, or available to, the attacker," 1Password said. Arguably more troubling is the revelation that the intruder gained access to 1Password's continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) infrastructure, which houses credentials used to keep its products running. The company says it has rotated or revoked potentially exposed credentials and that neither its apps nor its browser extensions were affected. 1Password hasn't explained how access to an employee's GitHub account enabled the attacker to deploy malicious code to its backend services, nor has it detailed the extent of the attacker's access to its software build and distribution infrastructure. The company did not respond to The Register's questions. The miscreant also got their hands on tokens embedded in emails sent to some customers as part of account invitations, provisioning, and recovery processes. These tokens aren't enough to access an account on their own, according to 1Password, as users must also authenticate via single sign-on or enter a verification code sent to their registered email address. The company says it specifically notified the small number of users with affected provisioning or recovery processes underway. It found no internal evidence of account takeovers using the exposed provisioning tokens. Still, the breach has prompted the password management biz to beef up those verification codes, replacing the six-digit numeric variety with ten-character alphanumeric codes to make brute-forcing them considerably more difficult. 1Password has booted the intruder out of its GitHub environment, revoked the stolen token, and rolled back the affected backend services to clean versions of the code. It's since shored up security around its development infrastructure and employees' devices, and brought in outside security specialists to review its handiwork. The incident recalls the first stage of LastPass's 2022 breach, when an attacker compromised its development environment and stole source code. technology.title: 45°C inlets just killed the chiller. Most people haven't noticed yet
technology.description: SC25 in St. Louis looked like a plumbing convention cross booked the supercomputing hall. Pipes, pumps, manifolds, quick-disconnects, and a lot of people who clearly spend more time thinking about pressure drop than floating-point. I kept expecting to see a booth selling industrial fire hoses. Chicago is a much bigger building – McCormick has roughly four times the exhibit space St. Louis had – so the pre-show question was whether SC26 will still look like that or whether the hall is large enough to dilute the effect. If anything, cooling was even more dominant in Chicago. The heat problem didn't get smaller just because the building got bigger. We also saw a lot of new companies displaying their cooling wares at SC26. I follow this stuff closely and see two broad trends. First: consolidation with big industrial suppliers buying up the liquid cooling pioneers. Second: anyone with an angle is heading into the market. Both trends were visible on the floor in Chicago, and everyone had something to say about higher inlet temperatures, whether they have a real story or not. Game changing news The real news, though, is a number Nvidia dropped earlier this year: 45°C (113°F) liquid inlet temperature for their parts. That's not a small tweak. Most liquid-cooled systems have been living in the 30-35°C (86-95°F) world because that's what the chips would tolerate. Jump to 45°C (113°F) and a whole bunch of datacenters that currently need chillers suddenly don't. If AMD, Intel, and the Arm folks can match it – and we’d be shocked if they aren't already working on exactly that – then free cooling stops being a cool climate thing and becomes the default for a lot of places. Rooftop dry coolers can reject nearly any incoming fluid temperature and bring it below 45°C (113°F). There are few places in the world where ambient temperatures approach 113°F, and for the hours when outside temps spike, adiabatic assist is available. This is where water is trickled through a mesh surrounding the dry coolers, which drops the effective temperature another 10–20 percent. So, in our new cooling world, there are two closed loops: one taking heat from the server gear and then passing it to a second, different loop that takes the hot water to the roof, cools it, then brings it back again. What's missing here? It's the chillers. You won't need them anymore. These are essentially huge rooftop refrigerators that cool water even more after the dry cooling. They're expensive, need a lot of maintenance, gulp electricity and are thankfully unnecessary now for new datacenter builds. The power and water savings are not trivial. Legacy designs that rely on chillers and open evaporative towers commonly put 20 percent to 40 percent of total facility energy into cooling. A large share of that is the chiller plant itself – compressors, pumps, and cooling-tower fans. Move to dry coolers running at 45°C (113°F) inlet and that slice collapses. technology.title: UK Home Office waved through border system without a working fix for bad data
technology.description: The Information Commission's Office (ICO) has reprimanded the UK Home Office over a border watchlist system launched without an effective way to correct inaccurate personal information. The regulator said the failings risked people being wrongly detained for additional checks at the UK border, potentially causing distress and other harm. The platform in question, Helios, was slated to replace its predecessor, Warnings Index, in September 2024 and despite an initial delay due to concerns over data quality, went live the following month. Both Helios and Warnings Index are watch-listing systems, designed to allow law enforcement officials – mainly but not exclusively Border Force – to check people's data against official records at the UK border. Helios's federated operating model, whereby the data sources are not centrally managed, yielded quicker results than Warnings Index, but contained a critical flaw in that operational staff could not alter incorrect records. Platform operators, such as Border Force officers, could not amend the data that feeds into it, neither after the fact nor in real time. This was not the case with Warnings Index, which had a dedicated team responsible for correcting data entries in real time. Under Helios, staff were supposed to report inaccuracies to the organization responsible for the relevant source data, which would make the correction. One slight problem: there was no established reporting system at the time Helios was launched on October 2. The platform went live anyway, as officials deemed the data integrity and security risks presented by Warnings Index to be greater than those of Helios. Just nine days passed before the Home Office's data protection officer had to submit a breach report after Helios operational staff said they didn't know how to request data corrections. During the time, Helios operators sent 87 data rectification requests to the Warnings Index correction team, despite it having no capability to make the required changes to the data. The Home Office later said that many other requests likely weren't logged as the proper processes were not in place, and that staff should have logged the issue through a ServiceNow IT ticket, as any other departmental civil servant with any kind of IT issue would have. But the Home Office also said that including personal data in those helpdesk tickets would itself constitute a data breach. The ICO said in its reprimand document [PDF] that it is "unclear" how such a reporting arrangement could realistically work in practice, given that a report would require details from a subject's record that required rectification as well as the new, accurate information that should be used to replace it. technology.description: The United States Federal Communications Commission has approved SpaceX’s plan to launch a million datacenter satellites. The regulator on Wednesday published an order [PDF] allowing SpaceX to operate a “Non-geostationary satellite orbit (NGSO) constellation of 1,000,000 satellites deployed into orbital shells each spanning 50 km at altitudes from 500 to 1,002 km and in 30-degree inclinations and sun-synchronous inclinations.” The order requires SpaceX to ensure its satellites’ radios don’t interfere with US government systems which use the 28.6-29.1 GHz band and requires the company to stick to operating within the parameters it files with the International Telecommunications Union. SpaceX asked the FCC to waive its rule requiring the atmospheric disposal of dead satellites orbiting at 2,000 km or less. Elon Musk’s company asked for “flexibility to dispose satellites operating above 600 km altitude into Earth disposal orbits or heliocentric orbits.” The FCC found SpaceX did not provide enough information to let it assess if proposed “alternative disposal methods” are compliant with regulations, so deferred its decision on the waiver request. “SpaceX must file an application for modification of this authorization and provide sufficient justification for any requested waiver(s) of the Commission’s rules,” the order states. The company must also file twice-yearly reports about “conjunction events” – moments when its satellites get dangerously close to each other, or other orbiters. Whether orbiting datacenters are feasible, make sense, or will ever pay for themselves, remain open questions. Analyst firm Gartner has described the idea as “ peak insanity .” Google thinks orbiting datacenters become viable if launch costs fall to $200/kg, which would mean SpaceX needs to launch its massive Starship 1,800 times. SpaceX’s assumptions assume near-daily launches, far better than its current cadence of a launch every three days or so. Fundamental networking research must also come to fruition to handle the amount of traffic large constellations of orbiting datacenters will create. Terrestrial manufacturing capacity will also need to increase to build all those satellites. Elon Musk’s companies and Intel have planned a giant new fab to make that possible, without explaining how the supply chains behind chip manufacturing will scale to make it feasible. That's a notable omission given that semiconductor supply chains are already extremely strained. Approval for SpaceX is therefore nice but in no way a roadmap to a million datacenter satellites. science.title: Space plants with hot sauce: What ISS astronauts will be eating on Thanksgiving (video)
science.description: null The astronauts on the International Space Station will celebrate Thanksgiving with some nontraditional fare. Well, NASA astronaut Anil Menon will, anyway. In a video the agency released on Monday (Nov. 23), Menon showed off some of the plants he and his crewmates are growing in orbit and told us what's in store for the greens. "We need plants to survive as we set up our moon base , and as we go to Mars , we're going to have to grow our own nutrition. So that's what we're doing this Thanksgiving," Menon said in the 2.5-minute video. Astronauts deliver a Thanksgiving message from the International Space Station in November 2026. From left: NASA's Luke Delaney and Anil Menon, the Canadian Space Agency's Joshua Kutryk and NASA's Jessica Watkins. (Image credit: NASA) "I plan on using this [plant] with a tortilla and some pasta and some hot sauce to make my Thanksgiving meal," added Menon, who was wearing a chef's toque for the occasion. "And I'm grateful for you and for my family at home." He passed the microphone to fellow NASA astronaut Luke Delaney, who didn't talk about food but expressed gratitude to his family, crewmates and support network on Earth . Next up was NASA's Jessica Watkins, who gave us a rundown of the broader Thanksgiving menu in space. "Some of what we'll be eating here — we've got some roasted turkey, some mac and cheese, some mashed potatoes, and some candied yams," Watkins said, showing off the small bags containing each of those comestibles. "So, we should be in good shape." The Canadian Space Agency 's (CSA) Joshua Kutryk spoke next. He said he'll eat rice and the space-grown plants, which he'll consume raw "because it reminds me of Earth, which I miss." All four of the astronauts then wished us a happy Thanksgiving and did some zero-g flips and rolls, sending the space plants on a bit of a ride. Delaney, Kutryk and Watkins are members of SpaceX's Crew-13 mission, which arrived at the International Space Station (ISS) on Oct. 1 . There's a fourth Crew-13 astronaut as well — Sergey Teteryatnikov, of the Russian space agency Roscosmos . That quartet shares the ISS with Menon and cosmonauts Pyotr Dubrov and Anna Kikina, who arrived in July aboard a Russian Soyuz spacecraft. Astronauts tend to get major holidays off on the ISS, and to celebrate them together. Doing so reinforces the already-strong bonds the crewmates share and helps them deal with the pain of being away from friends and family, which can be especially acute on holidays like Thanksgiving and Christmas. Kutryk is likely feeling especially emotional these days. On Tuesday, the CSA announced that Kutryk's wife had given birth to the couple's third child, a daughter. "Even with the distance between us, we feel incredibly connected as we welcome our new little star into our lives," the couple said in a statement shared by the CSA. "We are very proud of our growing family and are looking forward to getting our little crew of five all reunited."

science.description: Alzheimer’s disease, involving amyloid plaques in the brain, will be tough for AI to solve JUAN GAERTNER/SCIENCE PHOTO LIBRARY The progress AI has made in mathematics this year is nothing short of extraordinary. In January, I was impressed to see relatively minor open problems tackled with the help of AI . Now, AI is being used to solve the hardest problems in maths . The obvious next question is, if AI can do this, is there anything it can’t do? That is the inference that the AI companies want us to make, but, in reality, the answer is much more nuanced. Read more Mathematicians are amazed by ‘holy grail’ proof of Riemann hypothesis We see this messaging in claims that AI can “solve X”, where X is any field of human endeavour you care to name. Biology is a big one. “Cancer, Alzheimer’s, heart disease, mental illness – these will be relics of the past in, I think, less than a decade,” said Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei while promoting the company’s recent initial public offering . “I think one day maybe we can cure all disease with the help of AI,” said Demis Hassabis, CEO of Google DeepMind, last year , adding that this could be “within the next decade or so”. This phenomenon isn’t new: I call it “physicist brain”, after the propensity for physicists to wade into areas outside their expertise and declare simple solutions. More broadly, it is called Nobel disease , after the many Nobel prizewinners who have gone on to make, shall we say, less evidenced-backed claims. In general, there is a tendency to think that if an intelligent person is good at one thing, they are good at many other things that require intelligence. What is different now is that trillion-dollar companies and large swathes of the global economy now depend on this being true of artificial intelligence. Advertisement To be clear, I think we must now admit that AI is better at solving open mathematical problems than any human, and that this has happened faster than anyone ever expected. When I first saw the news in September that the Navier-Stokes problem had been solved by OpenAI , I felt stunned. We had entered a new world. With the announcement of the Riemann hypothesis proof this week, I felt sick and had to go and have a lie-down. These were intellectual Everests I have marvelled at since my teenage years, conquered by a machine far sooner than anyone expected. You may have read my recent piece forecasting the future in 2096 – an early draft had a line, later removed, about three Millennium Prize Problems being solved by AI in the 2030s. science.title: The defence tech revolution is changing how we innovate
science.description: Cpl Aaron J Stone/UK Ministry of Defence Only five years ago, defence technology start-ups had little choice but to wait for government funding to build and test their inventions – often in complex, multi-year programmes. No longer, however: Russia’s invasion of Ukraine in 2022 has prompted such a fast, furious response that military innovation timescales have shrunk dramatically. “Ukraine is becoming a real-world lab for military innovation, and it’s innovating at a pace greater than anything that we’ve seen previously,” says Ola Fashade, an air vice-marshal in the Royal Air Force and director of military digitalisation and the rapid AI delivery task force at the UK’s Ministry of Defence (MoD). “Agility and tempo of adaptation is critical. In a contested battlespace, technology that works well on day one, by day eight has become a little muted – and by day twelve it’s probably no longer relevant. And if you don’t adapt over that period, what you have is a very expensive and ineffective bag of steel.” Advertisement That raises the question of how significant this accelerated innovation could become. In September 2026, New Scientist CoLab, sponsored by BAE Systems, brought together leading thinkers and investors from industry, the military and academia to discuss the factors driving this innovation and the lessons that can be transferred to other industries. Staying alive The investment for this step change is coming both from the technology incubators based within military prime contractors – like the Launchpad incubator at BAE Systems – and from a host of venture capital (VC) companies worldwide. “The idea behind Launchpad is to forge an ecosystem that gets technology from defence start-ups into the front line quicker, or into spinouts, before they run out of money and die,” says David Ewing, head of technology commercialisation at BAE Systems. In addition, VC funding is seeing a raft of new multibillion-dollar military tech players, dubbed neoprimes, that complement the work of the primes on bigger-ticket battlespace items. The poster child for the neoprimes, says Samuel Burrell, a partner at the pan-European VC firm Expeditions Fund, is the nascent British air defence start-up Cambridge Aerospace, which reached a valuation of $3.4 billion with little but a convincing tech narrative: “They had no battlefield data, no product – just a compelling team and an idea on paper.” It wasn’t all talk: Cambridge Aerospace has begun delivering its Skyhammer air defence missile for taking out Shahed-type drones and cruise missiles. A solid-rocket-motor-powered ballistic missile interceptor, Starhammer, will ship in 2027. science.description: Earth Observatory Science Earth Observatory Seeking Refuge on Resolution… Earth Earth Observatory Image of the Day EO Explorer Topics All Topics Atmosphere Land Heat & Radiation Life on Earth Human Dimensions Natural Events Oceans Remote Sensing Technology Snow & Ice Water More Content Collections Global Maps World of Change Articles Earth Matters Blog Blue Marble: Next Generation EO Kids Mission: Biomes About About Us Subscribe 🛜 RSS Contact Us Search In the late 1800s, wildlife conservationists in New Zealand were recognizing how predators such as stoats , brought to the country to control other nonnative animal populations, were becoming a threat to native birds. Naturalists at the time surmised that some of the nation’s islands could serve as sanctuaries where endemic species could persist, free from the voracious newcomers. Resolution Island, located in the Fiordland region along the rugged southwest edge of New Zealand’s South Island, was one of the first eyed for this purpose. Conservationist Thomas Henry Potts proposed in 1872 that the island could be a place where “wingless species, and birds of feeble powers of flight, might there find a refuge for some of their representatives.” So began an early systematic effort to protect kiwi, kākāpō , and other native birds on Resolution Island, the largest of the approximately 90 islands in Fiordland National Park . This image, acquired with the OLI (Operational Land Imager) on Landsat 9 on December 12, 2025, shows the island’s setting amid a landscape of steep-sided valleys carved by glaciers and now inundated by the ocean. The uninhabited island rises from sea level to the summit of Mount Clerke at 1,069 meters (3,507 feet). Its diverse habitats and vegetation communities range from bogs and wetlands near the coast to widespread podocarp forests at middle elevations to tussock grasslands in the subalpine and alpine areas. Offshore, the Taumoana (Five Fingers Peninsula) Marine Reserve protects estuarine and wave-exposed rocky reef habitats at the entrance to Dusky Sound, east of Five Fingers Peninsula. Farther into the sound, Pigeon Island was the onetime home of Richard Henry, who was named caretaker of Resolution Island after it was designated a reserve in 1891. In what some have called a “ landmark effort ,” Henry spent years transporting more than 700 birds, mostly kiwi and kākāpō, by rowboat to Resolution and other would-be island sanctuaries nearby. In 1900, however, people began spotting mustelids on Resolution. It turns out the island is within swimming distance for animals such as stoats. Henry was intent on trapping the interlopers but eventually abandoned the project and moved on to caretaking work on another island. The spirit of his efforts lives on, though. A Department of Conservation program started in 2008 aims to control stoat populations and bolster native species on Resolution. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 25, 1970: NASA's 'wingless' M2-F3 'lifting body' aircraft makes its 1st powered flight ahead of supersonic tests
science.description: null On Nov. 25, 1970, an experimental aircraft called the Northrop M2-F3 made its first powered flight. The M2-F3 aircraft was a heavyweight "lifting body" designed to test its ability to produce most of its lift through its fuselage instead of wings. It's commonly referred to as a "wingless" aircraft. After Air Force test pilot Bill Dana took the M2-F3 on three unpowered glide test flights, he did the first powered flight, too. Dana soared to an altitude of 45,000 feet during this flight, which lasted just over 6 minutes. He didn't break the sound barrier this time, but he did on later flights. The M2-F3 flew a total of 27 missions in its three-year flight history. Its top speed was 1.6 times the speed of sound, and its top altitude was 71,500 feet. NASA's M2-F3 lifting body drops from its carrier plane during a test flight in 1970. (Image credit: NASA) Why it mattered In the late 1960s and early 1970s, NASA was investigating lifting bodies as an approach to both new aircraft and what future spacecraft, and as its number suggests, the M2-F3 was not the first of its kind. In fact, the M2-F3 was a rebuilt version of its predecessor, the M2-F2 lifting body , after that vehicle crashed in a dry lake bed in California's Mojave Desert during an unpowered test flight. That crash (which appears in the opening of the TV show "The Six-Million-Dollar Man") led to upgrades for a better handling lifting body, NASA said. "When the M2-F2 was rebuilt and redesignated the M2-F3, it was modified with an additional third vertical fin – centered between the tip fins – to improve control characteristics," NASA wrote in an overview . Unpowered glide flights for the M2-F3 began in June 1970, but Dana's flight on Nov. 25 of that year was the first time the vehicle fired up its rocket engine to test its controls under powered flight. One vital upgrade on the vehicle was a set of reaction control thrusters to help maintain its orientation. "A reaction jet control system, similar to thrusters used on orbiting spacecraft, was also installed on the M2-F3 to obtain research data about their effectiveness for vehicle control," NASA wrote . "As the M2-F3’s portion of the lifting body program neared an end, it evaluated a rate command augmentation control system and a side-arm control stick similar to side-arm controllers now used on many modern aircraft." If you want, you can see the M2-F3 vehicle today. NASA donated it to the Smithsonian Institution. It is now hanging at the National Air and Space Museum in Washington, D.C. Want more space history? science.title: Seabird ‘spies’ could help spot ships that aren’t broadcasting their location
